metadata.description: Navigable-water network for the Salish Sea and the BC Inside Passage: deep-water corridors, tidal passes, and an entrance spur for every harbour in the planner.
metadata.caution: A planning aid, not a chart. Corridors follow the middle of navigable water as OSM describes the shoreline; they carry no soundings and clear no rocks. Navigate from current charts.

properties.name: Puget Sound Main Channel
properties.note: Point No Point to Dalco Passage by way of East Passage — the deep, unobstructed spine of the Sound.

properties.name: Admiralty Inlet
properties.note: The Sound's front door. Ebb against a westerly in the Strait builds the steepest water on the route.

properties.name: Hood Canal
properties.note: Deep the whole way, but the floating bridge drawspan is the gate: 35 ft closed, opened on request to WSDOT on VHF 13.

properties.name: Rich Passage and Sinclair Inlet
properties.note: Narrow, buoyed, and busy with Bremerton ferries; the current runs hardest at the Point Glover bend.

properties.name: Port Orchard Passage
properties.note: The back way up the west side of Bainbridge, past Illahee and Brownsville to Agate Passage.

properties.name: Agate Passage
properties.note: 75 ft fixed bridge and up to 6 kn at springs — a slack-water passage for most masts.

properties.name: Port Washington Narrows and Dyes Inlet
properties.note: Two bascule bridges over a short, fast cut into Dyes Inlet.

properties.name: Colvos Passage
properties.note: Ebbs north almost all the time, which makes it the free ride from Tacoma towards Seattle.

properties.name: Tacoma Narrows
properties.note: 5.5 kn at springs under the twin bridges; a foul tide here costs more than the detour to wait for slack.

properties.name: South Sound Main Channel
properties.note: Narrows to Nisqually Reach past Steilacoom, keeping to the deep side of Ketron and Anderson Islands.

properties.name: Dana Passage
properties.note: The gate to Olympia and the western inlets; short, deep, and quick to build a tide rip.

properties.name: Budd Inlet
properties.note: Dredged and marked to Olympia at the head; leave the flats either side of the channel alone.

properties.name: Hammersley Inlet
properties.note: Four miles of narrow, winding, fast-running inlet to Shelton — a mid-channel, fair-tide passage.

properties.name: Balch, Drayton and Pitt Passages
properties.note: The inside route around Anderson and McNeil Islands, joining the Narrows channel to Carr Inlet.

properties.name: Hale Passage
properties.note: Between Fox Island and the Gig Harbor shore, under the Fox Island bridge.

properties.name: Elliott Bay and the Duwamish Waterway
properties.note: Commercial harbour: stay clear of the container berths and the ferry lanes at Colman Dock.

properties.name: Lake Washington Ship Canal
properties.note: Through the Ballard Locks into fresh water. Five opening bridges and one fixed 135 ft span; the Fremont Bridge at 30 ft closed is the binding one.

properties.name: Lake Washington
properties.note: Fresh water above the locks; no tide, and the only current worth the name is at the Montlake Cut.

properties.name: Possession Sound
properties.note: Round Possession Point wide — the tide rip off it stands up in any northerly.

properties.name: Saratoga Passage
properties.note: Deep and sheltered the whole length between Whidbey and Camano — the easy way north when Admiralty Inlet is up.

properties.name: Skagit Bay
properties.note: Shoal and shifting off the Skagit flats; the marked channel along the Whidbey shore is the only reliable water.

properties.name: Deception Pass
properties.note: 7+ kn at springs through a slot under a 180 ft bridge. Slack water only, and never against an ebb with a westerly outside.

properties.name: Swinomish Channel
properties.note: Dredged cut past La Conner joining Skagit Bay to Padilla Bay. 75 ft at the Rainbow Bridge, and it shoals at the south entrance.

properties.name: Port Townsend Canal
properties.note: The short cut from Port Townsend Bay to Oak Bay and Hood Canal. Fixed 58 ft span — tall rigs go round Marrowstone instead.

properties.name: Strait of Juan de Fuca
properties.note: Open ocean swell meets a strong tidal stream. A westerly against the ebb makes the eastern half stand up steeply on a summer afternoon.

properties.name: Race Passage
properties.note: Inside Race Rocks along the Vancouver Island shore — short, fast, and overfalls on a spring ebb.

properties.name: Victoria and Oak Bay
properties.note: Round Trial Island and Ten Mile Point well off; the tide sets hard across both.

properties.name: Haro Strait
properties.note: The deep international channel and the main shipping lane; whale traffic and freighters share it.

properties.name: Boundary Pass
properties.note: Turn Point to the Strait of Georgia. Deep, but the tide runs to 4 kn and freighters use it.

properties.name: Spieden Channel
properties.note: Links Haro Strait to San Juan Channel past Spieden Island; sets hard through the narrows at either end.

properties.name: Mosquito Pass and Roche Harbor
properties.note: Narrow and buoyed; the south end into Garrison Bay dries at the edges.

properties.name: San Juan Channel
properties.note: The islands' main street, Spieden Channel down to Cattle Pass past Friday Harbor.

properties.name: Cattle Pass
properties.note: The islands' south gate. Ebb against a Strait westerly stands up a genuinely dangerous sea off Cattle Point.

properties.name: Wasp Passage
properties.note: Threads the Wasp Islands; narrow, rock-strewn, and worth a chart rather than a memory.

properties.name: Rosario Strait
properties.note: The eastern deep-water route north. Tanker traffic to the Anacortes refineries, and a sharp rip off Lawrence Point on the ebb.

properties.name: Obstruction and Peavine Passes
properties.note: The east gate out of Orcas to Rosario Strait; either pass works, both run hard.

properties.name: President Channel
properties.note: Orcas's outside, between Waldron and the island's steep northwest shore.

properties.name: Thatcher Pass
properties.note: The ferry route in from Rosario Strait — the usual way into the islands from Anacortes.

properties.name: Burrows Pass
properties.note: The short way from Rosario Strait to Anacortes, between Fidalgo Head and Burrows Island.

properties.name: Guemes Channel
properties.note: Anacortes's waterfront channel; runs to 4 kn and the ferries turn in it.

properties.name: Padilla Bay
properties.note: Wide and shallow with a dredged refinery channel through it; the useful water is narrower than the bay looks.

properties.name: Bellingham Channel and Bellingham Bay
properties.note: Between Cypress and Guemes, then across to Bellingham past Eliza Island.

properties.name: Hale Passage, Lummi
properties.note: Inside Lummi Island to the Strait of Georgia; shoal at the north end off Lummi Point.

properties.name: Semiahmoo and Birch Bays
properties.note: Open, shoaling water along the Whatcom County shore up to the border at Blaine.

properties.name: Strait of Georgia
properties.note: Big open water with a short, steep chop when the wind opposes the tide. A northwesterly against an ebb off the Fraser is the classic bad afternoon.

properties.name: Active Pass
properties.note: Blind dogleg between Galiano and Mayne with BC Ferries in both directions and up to 7 kn. Call in on VHF 16 and keep hard to the starboard shore.

properties.name: Trincomali Channel
properties.note: The sheltered inside route up the Gulf Islands, Active Pass to Porlier.

properties.name: Porlier Pass
properties.note: Rock-strewn on both sides and up to 9 kn. Slack water and a good chart, or go round by Active Pass.

properties.name: Gabriola Passage
properties.note: Narrow, 8 kn at springs, and blind — a slack-water pass.

properties.name: Dodd Narrows
properties.note: A boat's-width of water at 9 kn springs. One direction at a time; log tows have priority and no options.

properties.name: Sansum Narrows
properties.note: Deep but squeezed between mountains; the wind funnels or dies altogether, and the tide runs both ways in the same hour.

properties.name: Stuart Channel
properties.note: Vancouver Island's inside road, Sansum Narrows up to Dodd, past Crofton, Chemainus and Ladysmith.

properties.name: Saanich Inlet
properties.note: A deep fjord with a shallow sill at the mouth; almost no tidal stream inside, and no swell ever.

properties.name: Fraser River, Steveston
properties.note: Sand Heads and the jetty channel. The river ebbs hard against a westerly and the bar breaks.

properties.name: Burrard Inlet
properties.note: English Bay anchorage, then First Narrows under Lions Gate at up to 6 kn, and Second Narrows beyond.

properties.name: Howe Sound
properties.note: Queen Charlotte Channel past Bowen Island. Squamish outflow winds blow hard down the sound in winter.

properties.name: Malaspina Strait
properties.note: Inside Texada Island — the sheltered lane up to Powell River when the Strait of Georgia is up.

properties.name: Sunshine Coast
properties.note: Gower Point to Welcome Passage along an exposed shore with few bolt-holes between Gibsons and Secret Cove.

properties.name: Jervis Inlet
properties.note: Sixty miles of steep-sided fjord with almost no anchorable bottom until the head.

properties.name: Malibu Rapids and Princess Louisa Inlet
properties.note: A one-boat-wide dogleg at slack only, then the finest anchorage on the coast at Chatterbox Falls.

properties.name: Sechelt Rapids
properties.note: The Skookumchuck: 16 kn and standing waves. Slack water is the only water.

properties.name: Baynes Sound
properties.note: Inside Denman Island to Comox; shoal at both ends and the Comox bar is buoyed for a reason.

properties.name: Discovery Passage
properties.note: Cape Mudge to Chatham Point past Campbell River. Everything here is timed off Seymour Narrows.

properties.name: Sutil Channel
properties.note: Between Cortes and Quadra — the road into Desolation Sound from the south.

properties.name: Desolation Sound
properties.note: Warm water, deep anchorages, and a lot of company in August. Almost no tidal stream once inside.

properties.name: Okisollo Channel, Surge Narrows and Hole in the Wall
properties.note: Beazley Passage at slack, then Okisollo's own rapids. Upper Rapids and Hole in the Wall each want their own slack.

properties.name: Yuculta, Gillard and Dent Rapids
properties.note: Three gates in a row on one slack. Get Gillard right and Dent follows; get it wrong and Devil's Hole is downstream of you.

properties.name: Arran Rapids
properties.note: The Bute Inlet gate — faster and less forgiving than the Yucultas.

properties.name: Cordero Channel
properties.note: The inside route from Dent to Johnstone Strait past Shoal Bay and Blind Channel, with Greene Point Rapids in the middle.

properties.name: Whirlpool Rapids and Wellbore Channel
properties.note: Short, steep, and best taken within twenty minutes of slack.

properties.name: Johnstone Strait
properties.note: Deep, straight and reliably windy: a summer westerly against the ebb builds a short steep sea that a small boat should be through before noon.

properties.name: Blackney Passage
properties.note: The gate from Johnstone Strait into the Broughtons; runs hard and is a favourite of the resident orca.

properties.name: Weynton Passage
properties.note: Out of Johnstone Strait to Alert Bay and Port McNeill; tide rips off the Stephenson Islets.

properties.name: Queen Charlotte Strait
properties.note: Opens to the Pacific swell at its western end. Port Hardy is the last full-service stop before Cape Caution.

properties.name: Fife Sound and the Broughton Archipelago
properties.note: The main way into the archipelago from Blackney; islands and reefs either side, so it is a chart-in-hand passage.

properties.name: Tribune Channel
properties.note: Round the back of Gilford Island past Kwatsi and Wahkana — steep-to, deep, and quiet.

properties.name: Chatham Channel and Knight Inlet approach
properties.note: Havannah Channel and the narrow, buoyed Chatham Channel cut through to Minstrel Island and Lagoon Cove.

properties.name: Inside Passage, Cape Caution to Prince Rupert
properties.note: Open to the Pacific across Queen Charlotte Sound and Milbanke Sound; sheltered in the channels between. A passage planned around weather windows, not around tides.
